en: The Ritual Manual for the Visualization of the Great Vidyā of the Mother of Buddhas, the Perfection of Wisdom, spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
Translated by the Dharma Master Śīladharma, recipient of the purple robe and subject, by imperial decree.
At that time, the World-Honored One [spoke] for the sake of all those practicing the supreme siddhi of the supramundane.
He proclaimed the visualization method for the Great Mantra of the Mother Prajñāpāramitā.
That mantra is as follows:

Namo bhagavate ārya-prajñāpāramitāyai | Aparimitāyur-nāthāyai | Bhakṣitavya-cārāyai | Sarva-tathāgata-jñāna-parivṛtāyai | Sattva-cārāyai | Tadyathā | Oṃ tre | Śrūti | Samiti | Vidyaye | Svāhā || This great vidyā possesses great merit.
This is the most supreme, most excellent,
and inconceivable method for practitioners of yoga who wish to visualize this great mantra-syllable in order to attain siddhi.
First, one should generate the mind of great awakening (bodhicitta).
Then, according to the ritual, one should visualize a pure moon disc upon one's own heart.
Within that moon disc, one should meditate on the syllable TI.
It revolves from the navel wheel and dwells in the heart.
This letter is yellow; it is the fundamental seed-syllable of the Bodhisattva Prajñāpāramitā.
Having visualized it in this manner:
Furthermore, one should visualize that these syllables immediately become the Bodhisattva Prajñāpāramitā.
One should visualize this Bodhisattva’s body as being of a true golden color, possessing six arms,
with all the marks and signs of perfection complete and adorned in various ways, and wearing a jeweled crown upon the head.
The supreme two hands form the *dharmacakra-mudrā*.
To form this seal, join the two palms together;
insert the two middle fingers within the palms so that their nail-faces are joined.
Place the two thumbs and the two index fingers together,
pressing their pads against one another;
with the remaining fingers unmoved, this constitutes the mudrā.
Other hands hold the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
utpala lotuses,
śakṭī flowers, and so forth.
Having visualized according to the ritual instructions in this manner,
one should again clearly contemplate the Great Mantra of the Prajñāpāramitā,
which is most supreme, profound, and born from non-self.
Because one observes that the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) is thus unborn and without self,
all phenomena are equal in their lack of self.
By virtue of this equality, [one realizes non-duality].
From this very Prajñāpāramitā, there arise the signs of infinite syllables.
As for these signs of syllables, they encompass all signs; if any practitioners of yoga hear them, [they shall attain realization].
If one hears "Oṃ" (唵引) and "Dhe" (提引), these two syllables should be visualized upon the crown of the head.
If one hears "Oṃ" (唵引) and "Ghe" (詣引), these two syllables should be visualized at the tip of the tongue.
Oṃ Āḥ. One should perform visualization upon the two ear-lobes for these two syllables.

Furthermore, if a practitioner of yoga wishes to visualize the mantra-syllables of this Mother Prajñāpāramitā, they should with sincere devotion visualize a great red eight-petaled lotus forming a maṇḍala upon their own heart. One should visualize the mantra-syllables distributed across the positions of the eight petals; these various syllables are not to be intermingled, but should be arranged and placed starting from the eastern petal of the lotus.
Visualize and arrange the two syllables NA and MO (Nāmo) in the position of the southeastern petal.
Visualize and arrange the four syllables VA-GA-VĀ-TE (Vāgavāte) in the position of the southern petal.
A-ri-ya-pra-ṇi-pa-ra-mi-tā-ye. Visualize these nine syllables as being arranged upon the petal in the southwest position.
Visualize the eight syllables *A-pa-ri-mi-ta-yu-na-ye* arranged upon the western petal.
Visualize the six syllables *Phat-kṛti-vaś-cara-ye* arranged upon the northwestern petal.
SARVA-TATHĀGATA-JÑĀNĀPARYUPTA-TE (14 syllables): Visualize these fourteen syllables as being arranged in the position of the northern petal.
Visualize the six syllables—*SA*, *TVA*, *VA*, *SA*, *RA*, and *YE*—arranged upon the petal in the northeast.
Then, having visualized these three syllables—*TAD*, *THA*, and *TA*—in sequence upon the positions of the eight petals, one should visualize them arranged in the center of the lotus.
Oṃ ti. Furthermore, visualize the distribution of eight positions within the surrounding area of the lotus;
visualize the single syllable *śru* (formed by the combination of two syllables) in the eastern position. Visualize [it] in the southeastern position.
Visualize the single syllable *ṭi* in the southern position.
Visualize *samari* (three-syllable compound) in the southwestern position.
Visualize the single syllable *ṭi* in the western position.
Visualize the single syllable *Vai* (ꉖ) in the northwest position;
visualize the single syllable *Ja* (ꉏ, pronounced with the "ren" and "zuo" initials) in the northern position;
visualize the single syllable *Ye* (ꉗ, with the extended vowel) in the northeast position.
Having thus visualized the two syllables of the great mantra, *Svāhā*,
and having duly arranged them, one should then,
according to the ritual, contemplate with focused attention the gateway of the ultimate truth of these syllables.
Alternatively, one may recite the mantra while maintaining mindfulness according to the ritual;
at the three times of the day, one should arrange the altar according to the rite and recite it one hundred and eight times.
Or one thousand and eighty recitations;
if performed for one month, six months,
or even up to one year without interruption.
One shall immediately attain the dharma of the most supreme and excellent siddhi.
Furthermore, whoever hears, upholds,
or recites it will become fully endowed with the power of hearing and retention, and shall realize the samādhi of emptiness.
Thus, this Great Mantra of the Mother of Buddhas, the Prajñāpāramitā,
is most supreme, profoundly deep, and possesses great merit.
A practitioner of yoga should perform visualization according to the ritual method in this manner.
The Ritual Manual for the Visualization of the Great Vidya of the Mother of Buddhas, the Perfection of Wisdom, as Spoken by the Buddha.
